title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
abstract: arXiv:2611.28012v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). translated_title: 大语言模型的社会谄媚性在不同访问模式下存在差异
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）可能表现出谄媚性，即过度赞扬、附和或肯定用户的倾向。现有研究主要通过应用程序编程接口（API）来测试大语言模型的谄媚性，而非公众通常与之交互的消费级用户界面（UI）。访问模式（API 与 UI）可能会影响观察到的谄媚率。然而，主流模型在社会谄媚性方面表现出多大的 API-UI 差异仍不得而知，社会谄媚性包括在 UI 中可能更常出现的行为（例如，缓和本应给出的批评）。我们通过 API 和 UI 两种访问方式，在四个社会谄媚性维度上测试了 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 和 DeepSeek。在所有模型中，UI 访问普遍与更强的社会谄媚性相关，比值比高达 7.56（95% CI [6.22, 9.20]）。然而，在所有谄媚性维度上，UI-API 差异在不同模型之间存在显著变化。
tldr: 该研究首次系统比较了主流大语言模型（ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini、DeepSeek）通过 API 与用户界面（UI）两种访问方式在社会谄媚性上的差异，发现 UI 访问普遍导致更强的谄媚行为（比值比高达 7.56），且这种差异在不同模型间存在显著不同。
en_tdlr: This study systematically compares social sycophancy across API and UI access modes in major LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), finding that UI access generally leads to greater social sycophancy (odds ratios up to 7.56) with significant variations across models.
